# Privacy policy

_Last updated: 25 November 2026_

Sparrow has no central server and no Sparrow account. The app talks to Control Planes and Community Nodes that independent operators run. This policy explains what stays on your phone, what those servers process, and where the limits are.

## What stays on your phone

- Your private encryption and signing keys. They never leave the phone, except inside an identity backup that you create and lock with your own password.
- Your messages, attachments, contacts, groups, polls, expenses and settings.
- Search by meaning, scam and phishing warnings, receipt scanning and voice transcripts. They are computed on your phone; message text is not sent to any AI service.

## What the servers process

- **Messages** wait end-to-end encrypted in mailboxes on a Community Node until your contact fetches them; **attachments** are stored there encrypted for a limited time. Envelopes are deleted after at most 7 days, mailboxes after at most 31 days. A mailbox stores nothing about who created it.
- **Your phone number**, so contacts can find you. The app registers it at its Control Planes, sealed so only their presence directory can read it. Community Nodes don't learn it.
- **Your public keys and routing IDs**, as far as delivery needs them.
- **Your network address.** Requests go through a route of community relays (Settings → Network → Onion routing). The first relay sees your address but not where the request goes; the last one sees the destination but not your address. While no route is available, the app sends directly unless you switch off "Send directly without a route".
- **Server logs** show the kind of request, not mailbox IDs, and are kept small.

## Exceptions you should know

- **Phone verification:** at sign-up, Google Firebase checks your number and sends the SMS, so Google processes your phone number for this.
- **First contact:** an invitation to someone whose key you don't have yet can't be encrypted. It contains your phone number, your public keys and an invite code.
- **Messages without encryption:** if a message is ever sent without encryption, an open lock appears next to its time.
- **Link previews and exchange rates** are fetched by the Community Node, so websites and the rate provider see the node's address, not yours.
- **Metadata:** servers can see when encrypted envelopes are stored and fetched, how large they are, and when your phone is online. Optional decoy envelopes make it harder to tell which mailboxes a message was for.

## What Sparrow doesn't do

- No ads, no tracking, no analytics and no crash reports.
- No push service: Sparrow keeps its own connection instead of using Firebase Cloud Messaging or similar.
- No selling of personal data.

## Your choices

- Clear all local data in Settings at any time. This deletes messages, contacts and keys on this phone and cannot be undone.
- Block contacts and invitations from unknown people.
- Switch the local intelligence features on or off.
- Choose how many relays, routes and decoy envelopes protect your messages.

## Contact

Sparrow is in beta. Questions about this policy: github.com/cbgm/Sparrow

# Data disclaimer

In plain terms: what Sparrow stores, where, and for how long.

## On your phone

- Your private encryption and signing keys, protected by the Android Keystore.
- Messages, attachments, contacts, groups, polls, expenses and pinned messages.
- Locally encrypted bank details, if you use settle-up.
- The local search model and index, if you switch on search by meaning.
- Your settings.

## On a Community Node (carries your messages)

- Encrypted envelopes until your contact fetches them, at most 7 days.
- Your mailboxes, at most 31 days. They contain nothing about you.
- Encrypted attachments, for a limited time until they are downloaded.
- Cached link previews and exchange rates. These contain no data about you.

## On a Control Plane (helps contacts find you)

- The signed list of Community Nodes.
- The link between your phone number and your device key, so contacts can find you. Only its presence directory can read your number.

## At Google Firebase

- Your phone number, while it is checked at sign-up.

## Your identity backup

- Contains your public identity and both private keys, encrypted with a password of at least 12 characters.
- Stored only where you save it. Your messages are not part of it.

## What servers can't read

- The content of encrypted messages and attachments.

## What servers can see

- When encrypted envelopes are stored and fetched, how large they are, and when your phone is online.
- The first relay of a route sees your network address. Without a route, the mailbox node sees it, unless you switch off "Send directly without a route".

## Clearing your data

You can clear all local data in Settings at any time. This removes messages, contacts and keys from this phone and cannot be undone. Data on servers expires by itself within the times above.

How many relays your connection runs through
Each relay only knows the one before and after it. More hops make you harder to trace, but slower and a little less reliable. They only help when the relays are run by different people.

Your contacts are spread across the circuits, each ending at a node of a different operator when there are enough, so no single operator sees all of them. Each circuit uses a little more battery and data.

With each message, this many decoys go into other contacts' mailboxes at the same moment, so a mailbox node cannot tell from timing whom you wrote to or who is in a group. They cost a little data for you and the contacts that get them; messages are not delayed. Sent only through a protecting circuit.
